# Tobi Lawson

> Tobi Lawson builds the software African businesses run on, and writes about capital, cities and how economies grow.

Every page is plain HTML with the full text in it, so fetching a URL is enough to read it. The main pages (home, about, writing, books, projects, course) also carry schema.org data in a JSON-LD script tag.

## Pages

- [Home](https://tobilawson.com/)
- [About](https://tobilawson.com/about/): Technology does not create economic value and prosperity, but it can be a positive force for public good.
- [Writing](https://tobilawson.com/writing/): Essays, book reviews, and field notes on capital, cities, and African development.
- [Books](https://tobilawson.com/books/): Who Made This? — a microhistory of everyday things, and other volumes in progress.
- [Projects](https://tobilawson.com/projects/): Companies and institutions Tobi Lawson has started or co-founded.
- [Course](https://tobilawson.com/course/): A free course on artificial intelligence for a general audience in Africa: how it works, who builds it, and what it means for work.

## Essays

- [Why Some Things Are Harder Than Others](https://tobilawson.com/writing/why-some-things-are-harder-than-others): Oct 2026. Difficulty often arises when an environment fails to make the right action clear, possible, or socially available.
- [Products Rule](https://tobilawson.com/writing/product-rules): Oct 2026. Why African tech companies should enter AI at the application layer.

## Books

- [WHO MADE THIS?: A microhistory of everyday things](https://tobilawson.com/books/): FORTHCOMING • IN WRITING. The stories behind 26 everyday objects, most of them part of daily life in Nigeria: the okada, the generator, garri, pure water, ankara, the jerry can and the plastic chair.
- [Read the first chapter free](https://tobilawson.com/books/chapter#book=who-made-this&chapter=01-the-okada)

## Projects

- [Briclair](https://briclair.com/): Fintech Infrastructure / Founder. Identity, accounts and compliance infrastructure for Nigerian fintechs.
- [Praiki](https://praiki.com/): Business Infrastructure / Founder. Infrastructure for African founders and professionals: vetted help, an operating layer for the business, and escrow that releases when the work ships.
- [Prai](https://prai.dev/): AI Workspace / Founder. An AI workspace for chat, code and agents.
- [Crapht](https://crapht.cloud/): Engineering Commons / Founder. An open commons for engineers who want to build hard things.
- [Fine Friction](https://finefriction.com/): Business Technology and Consulting / Co-founder. Technology products that help businesses leverage Artificial Intelligence.
- [Lagos Urban Project](http://lagosurban.com/): Platform / Founder. Reimagining Lagos as a more inclusive, livable, and productive city, built from how people live in it.
- [Long Africa](http://longafrica.org/): Institution / Launching Soon. An institution dedicated to the civilisational foundations of African prosperity across multi-decade horizons.
- [1914 Reader](https://www.1914reader.com/): Publication / Co-founder. A publication co-founded with Feyi Fawehinmi reading African stories through the lens of global economic change.

## Course

- How AI runs (Planned): The chips, data centres, power and connections AI depends on, and where Africa sits in that chain.
- The models (Planned): What a model is, how it learns from data, and why a handful of companies build most of them.
- The applications (Planned): The products built on top of models, and the problems they can and cannot solve yet.
- Work and disruption (Planned): Which jobs AI changes first, and what that means for workers and employers in African economies.
- The opportunities (Planned): Where Africans can build, invest and find work as AI spreads.
